draft.note_text:
Subjective: 57M with hx DM, HTN, asthma presenting with SOB x couple of weeks. Wakes up with SOB; SOB on exertion. Cough with hemoptysis x approx 3 weeks, pt reports 3-4 cups/day, only when coughing. Denies hematemesis, bleeding elsewhere, bruising or gum bleeding. No fevers. Denies leg swelling; chronic knee pain, longstanding, no swelling. Recent travel asked, not answered. No ED or hospital visits for this; could not get an earlier office appointment. DM: on metformin 500 mg BID, wears Dexcom; glucose up and down x approx 1 month, postprandial >200, fasting AM approx 150. Last HbA1c approx 7.7. HTN: on Norvasc but skips some days because home BP runs low, sometimes in the lower 90s.
Objective: SpO2 94%. BP 120/70. No JVD, no neck swelling, no carotid bruits. Lungs: rales and rhonchi, more on R; diminished breath sounds R; no wheezing. Heart: RRR, 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, unchanged from prior. Abdomen soft. Extremities: 1+ nonpitting edema bilateral ankles, no calf tenderness, negative Homan sign.
Assessment: 1. SOB with hemoptysis: lung findings suggest infection or other lung process, possibly pneumonia; concern for blood clot or something more serious. 2. DM: glucose running high. 3. HTN: BP running low at home on Norvasc.
Plan: 1. Refer to ED now for CXR, CT chest and blood work; clinician will call ED. Pt able to get to ED on his own. Treatment depending on findings. 2. Order HbA1c today. Will probably increase metformin from 500 mg BID to 750 mg BID. Return in approx 3 weeks to discuss diabetes and treatment plan once acute illness resolved. 3. Hold Norvasc for now; reassess BP once workup done and SOB under better control.

additions: Hemoptysis for approximately 3 weeks, patient-estimated at 3 to 4 cups per day, occurring only with coughing; denies hematemesis or bleeding elsewhere.
Medical Reasoning: Concern for a blood clot (pulmonary embolism) prompting CT of the chest; lung findings also suggest a possible infection.
Home blood pressure sometimes in the lower 90s; patient has been skipping Norvasc on some days because of low readings.
Shortness of breath for about 2 weeks, present on waking and with exertion.
Dexcom readings over about the past month: postprandial spikes well over 200, morning values around 150; last hemoglobin A1c approximately 7.7; current metformin 500 mg twice daily.
